top_five.text: An expanding Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused over 3,600 deaths among more than 7,500 confirmed cases, with health authorities warning the epidemic remains uncontrolled across seven provinces.
Twin earthquakes in north-central Venezuela have killed more than 160 people and injured nearly 1,000, prompting emergency search and rescue operations supported by international teams.
Widespread military strikes between the United States, Israel, and Iran have entered their eighth day following the death of top Iranian leadership, significantly increasing regional instability.
Internal displacement in Myanmar has escalated to nearly 3.8 million people, leaving an estimated 16.2 million individuals in urgent need of humanitarian aid.
Renewed fighting and Houthi offensives in Yemen have displaced more than 112,000 people over two weeks and caused thousands to cross the Red Sea into neighboring Djibouti.

top_story.quote: An expanding Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has resulted in over 3,600 deaths across seven provinces as health officials warn the epidemic is far from being contained.
top_story.label: AFRICA — Expanding Ebola Outbreak

Middle East.headline: Middle East — Regional conflict escalates as US, Israel, and Iran trade airstrikes
Middle East.body: A major regional military conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran has entered its eighth day following a joint US-Israeli strike on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and military commanders. Tehran launched retaliatory attacks, while fresh airstrikes targeted the Iranian capital. Amid the escalating hostilities, the US administration approved a 151 million USD arms sale to Israel as drone and missile attacks continue across the region.
verified_figures: 151 million US dollar arms sale approved

Middle East.headline: Yemen / Saudi Arabia — Houthi offensive triggers mass displacement and cross-border attacks
Middle East.body: Fighting between Houthi rebels and government forces in Yemen has displaced over 112,000 people in two weeks, according to the UN, straining humanitarian capacity near Aden. Houthi forces seized control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Hanish Islands, while recent clashes killed 48 people. Missile and drone attacks directed at Saudi Arabia caused explosions near Riyadh airport and flight disruptions, leading the US to evaluate strike options against Houthi targets. Additionally, IOM reported that thousands of displaced individuals have crossed into Djibouti.
verified_figures: more than 112,000 people displaced in the past two weeks

Middle East.headline: Gaza — Israeli airstrikes kill four Palestinians including a child
Middle East.body: Israeli military strikes in Gaza killed at least four Palestinians on Saturday, including a child and the son of Gaza's health ministry director-general. The casualties occurred amidst an ongoing severe humanitarian crisis in Gaza, while demonstrations in Tunisia called for the release of detained Gaza Flotilla activists.

Americas.headline: Venezuela — Deadly twin earthquakes cause major casualties in north-central region
Americas.body: A pair of powerful earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela on Wednesday evening, causing extensive casualties and structural damage. As of Thursday morning, more than 160 people have been killed and nearly 1,000 others injured. Emergency responders are carrying out intensive search and rescue operations to locate individuals trapped under rubble. Acting President Delcy Rodriguez stated that rescue operations are underway, while the United States confirmed it is sending search and rescue teams to assist local authorities with ongoing relief efforts.

Americas.headline: United States/Haiti — Termination of Temporary Protected Status leaves 330,000 Haitians facing deportation
Americas.body: The revocation of Temporary Protected Status in the United States has placed approximately 330,000 Haitians at risk of deportation, alongside several thousand nationals from Syria, Somalia, Ethiopia, and Sudan following policy decisions made in February. The removal of legal protections raises protection concerns for vulnerable migrants. The decision also directly impacts essential workforces across multiple U.S. states, particularly in healthcare, nursing homes, remediation centers, agriculture, and local service industries.

Africa.headline: DR Congo — Ebola outbreak expands across provinces as test vaccination program launches
Africa.body: Doctors Without Borders has warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to spread to new areas, including North Kivu province, despite reduced transmission in the initial epicenter of Ituri. Official figures report 3,639 deaths among 7,541 confirmed cases across seven provinces. UN Women highlighted that women and girls face disproportionate risk due to traditional caregiving roles in homes and health facilities. In response, health authorities, supported by WHO and MSF, have launched a test vaccination drive among frontline health personnel to evaluate whether a vaccine designed for a different strain can effectively contain the virus.
verified_figures: 20,000 health personnel enrolled in one-year clinical trial

Europe.headline: Russia/Ukraine — Major drone attack targets Moscow region, killing two
Europe.body: Russian authorities reported a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack targeting Moscow and the surrounding region, resulting in at least two deaths and damage to a major oil refinery. According to local officials, air defense systems intercepted more than 1,600 drones in total, including 450 aimed directly at the Russian capital. Moscow's mayor characterized the strike as the largest drone attack on the capital to date. The strikes coincided with the final day of voting in Russia's parliamentary election.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Recruitment of minors by Russian forces highlights child protection concerns
Europe.body: At least 13 Ukrainian minors are currently imprisoned in Ukraine after being recruited and paid by Russian entities to conduct attacks inside their own country. The recruitment and exploitation of children by combatants highlights growing protection risks faced by vulnerable youth during the conflict.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar — Internal displacement reaches nearly 3.8 million
Asia-Pacific.body: According to a mid-year report released by UNICEF citing UNHCR figures, nearly 3.8 million people were internally displaced across Myanmar by the end of June. The total of 3,793,800 internally displaced persons represents an increase of 154,400 compared to the end of 2025. In total, an estimated 16.2 million people across the country, including 4.9 million children, require humanitarian assistance due to ongoing conflict and widespread instability.
verified_figures: 154,400 increase in displaced persons since end-2025
16.2 million people in need of humanitarian assistance

Asia-Pacific.headline: Pakistan — Dozens killed and injured in northwestern armed attack
Asia-Pacific.body: Dozens of people were killed and injured following an attack by an armed group in a northwestern city in Pakistan. The violence highlights the continuing threat posed by recurrent bombings and insurgent activities in the region, creating severe protection concerns and volatile security conditions for local civilian populations.

Asia-Pacific.headline: India — Rohingya families rendered homeless following Jammu eviction drive
Asia-Pacific.body: An eviction drive in the Karyani Talab area of Narwal in Jammu has left hundreds of Rohingya refugee families homeless. Local authorities instructed landowners to vacate plots rented to refugee families, leading to the removal of 30 to 40 shops and the dismantling of makeshift shelters. An estimated 350 to 500 families living in 80 to 90 huts were affected, with many having resided in the area for up to 16 years.

Asia-Pacific.headline: India — Study warns of rapid Himalayan glacier melt in Uttarakhand
Asia-Pacific.body: A study conducted by scientists at the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology and published in Discover Geoscience found that 23 major glaciers in Uttarakhand are melting rapidly. Researchers attributed the accelerated melting directly to rising temperatures driven by climate change and global warming, warning that the loss of glacial ice increases long-term regional flood risks.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Health: Ebola outbreak not yet under control, CDC warns
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: ________________ An Ebola outbreak in DR Congo was far from being "under control", Africa's top health body said Thursday, a day after the WHO said it was gaining ground against the virus. The outbreak, which began in the conflict-scarred northeastern province of Ituri, has seen more than 3,500 deaths from over 7,200 cases to date across seven northern and eastern provinces. The Africa Centrer for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) director general Jean Kaseya acknowledged there had been a "plateau" in cases, adding they were seeing "a slight decrease". Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Nepal: Cholera Risk Rises in Nuwakot After Floods, Oral Vaccines to Be Administered to ...
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Kathmandu, 20 September (H.S.): The threat of a cholera outbreak has increased in Nepal’s Nuwakot district following the recent floods, prompting the launch of an oral cholera vaccination campaign. Under the campaign, more than 50,000 people have already been vaccinated. The authorities have set a target of vaccinating more than 77,000 people in the affected areas. The campaign has been launched by the District Public Health Office, Nuwakot, in coordination with the Epidemiology and Disease Control Division.
